newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX charges ahead as U.S. rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: German DAX charges ahead as U.S. rates unchanged.

text.p: German shares rallied on Wednesday as traders and investors were wrong-footed by the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to leave interest rates unchanged.
"As negative as everything looked yesterday, it's all positive today," a Frankfurt trader said of a rally that pushed the blue chip DAX index up 1.5 percent.

The 30-share DAX ended the bourse session up 52.66 points at 3,596.09, boosted in particular by strong interest in chemicals and metals firm Degussa, in which utility Veba bought a 36.4 percent stake at a high premium to its traded price.
Degussa ended the day up 8.80 marks, or 11.6 percent, at 84.80 marks, surging after Veba said earlier it had bought the stake at 86.80 marks per share.

The deal, which is expected to lead to strategic link-ups between Veba's Huels unit and Degussa, was viewed as positive for both companies, especially as Veba said it will not have to raise capital to finance the deal.
Thomas Deser of BHF Bank raised Veba to a buy from hold and raised its earnings per share forecast by 10 pfennigs over each of the next two years to 5.70 marks in 1997 and 6.30 marks in 1998.

Christine Dienhart, chemicals analyst at Bayerische Vereinsbank in Munich, added: "This is very positive news. The best part is the 86.80 marks per share price paid, which confirms that our own long-term target for the share of 92.50 marks is in the right area."
Bank shares also rallied, with the DAX-100 bank shares index clocking up gains of 2.6 percent.

Dealers linked their gains partly with the Veba-Degussa deal, since Dresdner Bank AG was among three companies who sold Degussa stock and stands to gain 789 million marks from the deal. Dresdner rose 3.2 percent to 62.35 marks.
Dealers said news of the acquisition may have boosted hopes that German banks were poised to offload more of their industrial shareholdings.
